title: x86 Architecture — Detailed Machine-Readable Knowledge Graph
description: A detailed entity-and-relationship graph for the x86 instruction set architecture family, including history, execution modes, registers, instruction encoding, addressing, ISA extensions, memory translation, ABI/toolchains, virtualization, security, and performance.

source_context.primary_user_supplied_source: Pasted text describing the x86 Wikipedia article, including overview, chronology, properties, register sets, modes, extensions, and modern ecosystem initiatives.
source_context.scope_note: Source-derived facts are represented alongside general architectural organization needed to connect the concepts. Feature support varies by CPU model, execution mode, operating system, and enabled extended state; do not treat every extension as universal.

metadata.relationship_endpoint_policy: Every source and target must refer to an existing entity id.
coverage: real, protected, virtual-8086, SMM, and long-mode states
segmentation, paging, virtual memory, exceptions, interrupts
object formats, assemblers, compilers, linkers, loaders, ABIs
SIMD, floating point, crypto, matrix, random, and bit-manipulation extensions
performance, speculation, multicore, memory ordering, and security

entities.name: x86 architecture
entities.description: A historically extended family of Intel-origin CISC instruction-set architectures, commonly including IA-32 and x86-64.

entities.name: Instruction set architecture
entities.description: Programmer-visible contract defining instructions, registers, exceptions, and architectural state.

entities.name: Microarchitecture
entities.description: Internal processor implementation that realizes the ISA; different CPUs can implement the same x86 ISA differently.

entities.name: Machine code
entities.description: Binary instruction encodings consumed by an x86 processor.

entities.name: x86 assembly language
entities.description: Human-readable mnemonic and operand notation assembled into x86 machine code.

entities.name: Assembler
entities.description: Translates assembly source into object code or machine-code bytes.

entities.name: Compiler
entities.description: Translates a high-level language into machine code, often through intermediate representations and instruction selection.

entities.name: Linker
entities.description: Combines object files and libraries, resolves symbols, and applies relocations.

entities.name: Program loader
entities.description: Maps executable segments, prepares runtime state, and transfers control to program entry.

entities.name: Application binary interface
entities.description: Defines calling conventions, data layout, register preservation, stack alignment, symbol conventions, and binary interoperability.

entities.name: Operating system
entities.description: Manages processes, virtual memory, scheduling, privilege, interrupts, and device access.

entities.name: System firmware
entities.description: Boot-time and platform code such as BIOS/UEFI; early startup often begins in real mode on compatible processors.

entities.name: x86-compatible CPU
entities.description: Processor implementing one or more x86 architectural modes and feature subsets.

entities.name: Intel
entities.description: Original designer of the 8086 family and major x86 ISA steward.

entities.name: AMD
entities.description: Designer of the x86-64/AMD64 extension later implemented compatibly by Intel.

entities.name: Binary compatibility
entities.description: Ability to execute existing binaries under a compatible architectural and ABI environment.

entities.name: CPUID and feature detection
entities.description: Mechanisms used by software to identify processor capabilities and supported ISA extensions.

entities.name: Microarchitectural performance
entities.description: Observed execution performance determined by implementation, workload, memory hierarchy, and instruction mix.

entities.name: x86 security mechanisms
entities.description: Architectural and microarchitectural controls affecting isolation, memory permissions, speculation, and execution privilege.

entities.name: Hardware virtualization
entities.description: Processor facilities allowing a hypervisor to run and control guest operating systems.

entities.name: Memory and ordering model
entities.description: Rules governing loads, stores, atomicity, ordering, and visibility across cores.

entities.name: Interrupts and exceptions
entities.description: Events that transfer execution to privileged handlers, with architectural state saved according to the mode and event type.

entities.name: I/O mechanisms
entities.description: Memory-mapped I/O and legacy port-mapped I/O mechanisms available on applicable modes/platforms.

entities.name: Paging
entities.description: Maps linear/virtual addresses to physical addresses through hierarchical page tables and permissions.

entities.name: Segmentation
entities.description: Segment-based address translation and protection, central in 16-bit modes and retained in modified form in later modes.

entities.name: Architectural registers
entities.description: Program-visible general, control, status, segment, debug, floating-point, and vector registers.

entities.name: RFLAGS/EFLAGS/FLAGS
entities.description: Status and control flag state used by arithmetic, branches, and system control.

entities.name: General-purpose registers
entities.description: Integer registers used for arithmetic, data movement, addressing, and ABI-defined argument/return roles.

entities.name: SIMD and vector execution
entities.description: Packed-data execution that performs the same operation across multiple lanes.

entities.name: Floating-point execution
entities.description: x87 stack-based floating-point operations and later scalar/vector floating-point facilities.

entities.name: Memory hierarchy
entities.description: Architectural memory addresses backed by caches, RAM, and device mappings.

entities.name: CPU caches
entities.description: Fast memory hierarchy that stores instructions and data close to execution units.

entities.name: Instruction pipeline
entities.description: Stages that fetch, decode, schedule, execute, and retire instructions.

entities.name: Micro-operations
entities.description: Internal operations into which many complex x86 instructions are decoded by modern implementations.

entities.name: Branch prediction
entities.description: Predicts control-flow outcomes to keep speculative execution supplied with work.

entities.name: Out-of-order execution
entities.description: Allows independent operations to execute when ready rather than strictly in program order, while preserving architectural retirement semantics.

entities.name: Speculative execution
entities.description: Executes predicted paths before their correctness is known; architectural results are committed or discarded as appropriate.

entities.name: Register renaming
entities.description: Maps architectural registers to internal physical registers to remove false dependencies.

entities.name: In-order retirement
entities.description: Commits completed operations in architectural order, preserving precise visible state.

entities.name: Exception
entities.description: Synchronous event caused by instruction execution, such as divide error, invalid opcode, or page fault.

entities.name: Fault
entities.description: Exception generally reported with restart semantics at the faulting instruction.

entities.name: Trap
entities.description: Exception reported after an instruction has completed its defined action.

entities.name: Abort
entities.description: Exception class for severe conditions where restart position may be unreliable.

entities.name: Intel 8080 ancestry
entities.description: 8-bit predecessor lineage that influenced the 8086 design.

entities.name: Intel 8086
entities.description: Introduced in 1978; 16-bit architecture with segmented addressing.

entities.name: Intel 8088
entities.description: 8086-compatible CPU with an 8-bit external data bus; used in the original IBM PC.

entities.name: Intel 80186/80188
entities.description: 8086-family successors integrating additional platform peripherals.

entities.name: Intel 80286
entities.description: Added protected mode and expanded physical addressing relative to 8086.

entities.name: Intel 80386
entities.description: Introduced IA-32 32-bit registers, 32-bit addressing, and paging support.

entities.name: Intel 80486
entities.description: Added more integrated execution facilities, pipelining, cache, and on-chip FPU in DX models.

entities.name: Intel Pentium / P5
entities.description: Superscalar generation; later Pentium MMX added packed integer SIMD.

entities.name: Intel Pentium Pro
entities.description: Introduced advanced dynamic execution and PAE-era capabilities.

entities.name: Pentium II / Pentium III
entities.description: Successors adding cache/package variants and SSE in Pentium III.

entities.name: Intel Pentium 4
entities.description: NetBurst microarchitecture; introduced SSE2 and later SSE3 in product evolution.

entities.name: Intel Core family
entities.description: Core-era designs with wide dynamic execution, fusion, and evolving vector extensions.

entities.name: Intel Xeon
entities.description: Server/workstation x86 processors spanning multiple microarchitectures and features.

entities.name: Intel Atom
entities.description: Low-power x86 processor family used in selected embedded and compact systems.

entities.name: AMD Opteron
entities.description: Early mass-market x86-64 processor family introduced in 2003.

entities.name: AMD Athlon
entities.description: Important AMD x86 family preceding and overlapping the x86-64 era.

entities.name: AMD Ryzen
entities.description: Modern AMD x86-64 client processor family.

entities.name: AMD EPYC
entities.description: AMD x86-64 server processor family.

entities.name: Zhaoxin x86 processors
entities.description: VIA-derived x86-compatible processors developed by Zhaoxin.

entities.name: Transmeta Crusoe/Efficeon
entities.description: x86-compatible processors using dynamic binary translation to a VLIW implementation.

entities.name: Intel Itanium / IA-64
entities.description: Distinct EPIC/IA-64 architecture, not x86 ISA, with limited x86 emulation support.

entities.name: X86S proposal
entities.description: Intel proposal to simplify legacy modes; source states the proposal was abandoned in 2024.

entities.name: x86 Ecosystem Advisory Group
entities.description: Intel/AMD-led group formed in 2024 to improve consistency and standardize interfaces/features.

entities.name: Real mode
entities.description: 8086-compatible segmented execution, typically 20-bit physical address formation and no hardware-enforced process isolation.

entities.name: Unreal mode
entities.description: Informal mode using real-mode execution with selected cached descriptor attributes from protected mode.

entities.name: Protected mode
entities.description: Mode introduced on 80286 with privilege, descriptor-based segmentation, and later paging support.

entities.name: Virtual 8086 mode
entities.description: 80386 protected-mode submode allowing 8086-style tasks under a protected-mode supervisor; not available in long mode.

entities.name: System Management Mode
entities.description: Privileged firmware-oriented mode using SMRAM for system-management handlers.

entities.name: Long mode
entities.description: x86-64 operating state comprising 64-bit submode and compatibility submode.

entities.name: 64-bit mode
entities.description: Native x86-64 execution submode with 64-bit GPRs and RIP-relative addressing.

entities.name: Compatibility mode
entities.description: Runs many 16-/32-bit protected-mode applications under a 64-bit operating system.

entities.name: Legacy mode
entities.description: x86-64 processor state for traditional real/protected/virtual-8086 execution environments.

entities.name: Privilege rings
entities.description: Architectural privilege levels 0 through 3; most general-purpose operating systems use ring 0 for kernel and ring 3 for applications.

entities.name: Ring 0
entities.description: Highest privilege level in the conventional x86 ring model.

entities.name: Ring 3
entities.description: Least privileged conventional level, commonly used for applications.

entities.name: RAX/EAX/AX/AL/AH
entities.description: Accumulator register with overlapping 64-, 32-, 16-, and legacy high/low-byte views.

entities.name: RBX/EBX/BX/BL/BH
entities.description: General-purpose/base register with legacy high/low-byte aliases.

entities.name: RCX/ECX/CX/CL/CH
entities.description: Counter register; used by loop/string instructions and ABI-dependent arguments.

entities.name: RDX/EDX/DX/DL/DH
entities.description: Data/extension register; paired with accumulator in selected multiply/divide operations.

entities.name: RSI/ESI/SI/SIL
entities.description: Source-index register; also general purpose in modern modes.

entities.name: RDI/EDI/DI/DIL
entities.description: Destination-index register; also general purpose in modern modes.

entities.name: RBP/EBP/BP/BPL
entities.description: Base/frame pointer register; general purpose where not reserved by ABI/compiler.

entities.name: RSP/ESP/SP/SPL
entities.description: Stack pointer; points to the current stack top according to stack convention.

entities.name: RIP/EIP/IP
entities.description: Instruction pointer/program counter.

entities.name: R8–R15
entities.description: Eight additional 64-bit general-purpose registers introduced by x86-64; byte/word/dword aliases are available.

entities.name: R16–R31
entities.description: Extended GPRs in APX-capable implementations; availability is feature-specific.

entities.name: CS, DS, SS, ES, FS, GS
entities.description: Segment selector registers; FS/GS can remain useful for thread-local or system-specific bases.

entities.name: FLAGS/EFLAGS/RFLAGS
entities.description: Flag register widths across generations; includes arithmetic status and system control bits.

entities.name: CR0–CR4 and CR8 where supported
entities.description: Control registers configure protected mode, paging, protection, and selected system features.

entities.name: DR0–DR3, DR6, DR7
entities.description: Hardware breakpoint and debug status/control registers.

entities.name: GDTR, LDTR, IDTR, TR
entities.description: Descriptor-table and task-register state used by protected-mode system software.

entities.name: Model-specific registers (MSRs)
entities.description: Implementation/feature-specific control and status registers accessed by privileged instructions.

entities.name: Test registers TR3–TR7
entities.description: Legacy 80486-era test registers; not general modern application registers.

entities.name: ST(0)–ST(7)
entities.description: Eight 80-bit x87 floating-point stack registers.

entities.name: MM0–MM7
entities.description: Eight 64-bit packed-integer registers aliased to the x87 register file.

entities.name: XMM0–XMM31
entities.description: 128-bit SIMD registers; count depends on mode and supported extensions.

entities.name: YMM0–YMM31
entities.description: 256-bit AVX-family vector register views; lower 128 bits correspond to XMM views.

entities.name: ZMM0–ZMM31
entities.description: 512-bit AVX-512 vector register views; availability and count depend on mode/features.

entities.name: K0–K7
entities.description: AVX-512 opmask registers controlling per-lane predication and masking.

entities.name: MXCSR
entities.description: SSE floating-point control/status register.

entities.name: XCR0 and extended state control
entities.description: OS-managed extended-state configuration used with XSAVE-family mechanisms.

entities.name: XSAVE-managed extended state
entities.description: Mechanism family for saving/restoring extended SIMD, x87, and other processor state.

entities.name: Instruction prefixes
entities.description: Legacy, operand-size, address-size, segment, REP/LOCK, REX, VEX, XOP, and EVEX-related prefixes modify decoding or semantics.

entities.name: REX prefix
entities.description: 64-bit-mode prefix that selects 64-bit operand size and/or extended register encodings.

entities.name: VEX prefix
entities.description: Two-/three-byte encoding prefix used by AVX and related vector instructions.

entities.name: EVEX prefix
entities.description: Extended encoding scheme used by AVX-512 and selected newer extensions.

entities.name: REX2 prefix
entities.description: Two-byte prefix scheme associated with APX extended general-purpose register encoding.

entities.name: Opcode
entities.description: Instruction encoding field identifying an operation or opcode family.

entities.name: ModR/M byte
entities.description: Encoding byte describing operand form, register selection, and memory/register mode.

entities.name: SIB byte
entities.description: Scale-index-base encoding byte used by many 32-/64-bit effective addresses.

entities.name: Displacement field
entities.description: Signed or unsigned encoded offset added to an effective address or branch target.

entities.name: Immediate operand
entities.description: Constant encoded in the instruction stream.

entities.name: Register operand
entities.description: Operand located in an architectural register.

entities.name: Memory operand
entities.description: Operand accessed through an effective address.

entities.name: Relative branch displacement
entities.description: Encoded displacement relative to the next instruction or architecture-defined instruction pointer.

entities.name: 16-bit addressing forms
entities.description: Classic combinations of BX/BP with SI/DI plus displacement and segment selection.

entities.name: 32-bit addressing forms
entities.description: Base + index*scale + displacement effective address using 32-bit registers.

entities.name: 64-bit addressing forms
entities.description: Extended base/index addressing, RIP-relative addressing, and FS/GS base use in 64-bit mode.

entities.name: RIP-relative addressing
entities.description: Memory address formed relative to RIP plus displacement, useful for position-independent code.

entities.name: Base-index-scale addressing
entities.description: Effective address based on base + index × scale + displacement; scale commonly 1, 2, 4, or 8.

entities.name: Segment override
entities.description: Prefix selecting a segment register where applicable.

entities.name: Operand-size attribute
entities.description: Selects operation operand width, subject to mode defaults and prefixes.

entities.name: Address-size attribute
entities.description: Selects effective-address calculation width, subject to mode defaults and prefixes.

entities.name: LOCK prefix
entities.description: Requests a locked/atomic memory operation for instructions and operand forms that support it.

entities.name: REP/REPE/REPNE prefixes
entities.description: Repeat string operations according to count and, where relevant, comparison flags.

entities.name: Data movement
entities.description: MOV, MOVZX, MOVSX/MOVSXD, XCHG, LEA, PUSH, POP and related transfer operations.

entities.name: Integer arithmetic
entities.description: ADD, ADC, SUB, SBB, INC, DEC, NEG, MUL, IMUL, DIV, IDIV and related operations.

entities.name: Logical and bit manipulation
entities.description: AND, OR, XOR, NOT, TEST, shifts, rotates, bit tests and bit-field operations.

entities.name: Compare and conditional control flow
entities.description: CMP, TEST, Jcc, SETcc, CMOVcc and related flag-dependent behavior.

entities.name: Control transfer
entities.description: JMP, CALL, RET, LOOP, indirect branches, far transfers, and return control flow.

entities.name: String operations
entities.description: MOVS, CMPS, SCAS, LODS, STOS and REP-prefixed forms.

entities.name: Stack operations
entities.description: PUSH/POP, CALL/RET stack effects, and stack-pointer conventions.

entities.name: Atomic and synchronization operations
entities.description: LOCK-prefixed operations, XCHG, CMPXCHG, XADD, and related synchronization primitives.

entities.name: System instructions
entities.description: Instructions controlling privilege, tables, interrupts, timing, CPU identification, and system state.

entities.name: Port I/O instructions
entities.description: IN, OUT, INS, OUTS where supported and permitted.

entities.name: x87 floating-point instructions
entities.description: Floating-point stack arithmetic, loads/stores, comparisons, conversions, and transcendental operations.

entities.name: SIMD/vector instructions
entities.description: Packed integer, floating-point, shuffle, permutation, gather/scatter, and lane operations.

entities.name: Cryptographic instructions
entities.description: AES, carry-less multiplication, SHA and other optional cryptographic acceleration instructions.

entities.name: Random-number instructions
entities.description: RDRAND and RDSEED where supported; feature detection and failure/status handling are required.

entities.name: Bit manipulation extensions
entities.description: POPCNT, LZCNT, BMI-family and ADX operations when implemented.

entities.name: Matrix/tile instructions
entities.description: AMX/tile-oriented matrix operations and related state management where supported.

entities.name: Transactional memory
entities.description: TSX-related transactional memory instructions on implementations that support them.

entities.name: Virtualization instructions
entities.description: VMX and SVM instruction families and supporting state.

entities.name: Cache and prefetch instructions
entities.description: Cache management, prefetch hints, and ordering instructions.

entities.name: Memory fence instructions
entities.description: LFENCE, SFENCE, MFENCE and related ordering mechanisms.

entities.name: System-call transition instructions
entities.description: SYSCALL/SYSRET and SYSENTER/SYSEXIT mechanisms, with mode/OS conventions.

entities.name: Interrupt control instructions
entities.description: INT, IRET, CLI, STI and related event/interrupt operations, subject to privilege and mode.

entities.name: x87 FPU extension
entities.description: Floating-point coprocessor lineage with 80-bit stack registers and extended-precision operations.

entities.name: Physical Address Extension (PAE)
entities.description: Paging format extension allowing 32-bit protected-mode systems to address physical memory beyond 4 GiB on supporting platforms.

entities.name: NX/XD bit
entities.description: Execute-disable page permission used to reduce exploitation of data pages as executable code.

entities.name: MMX
entities.description: 64-bit packed-integer SIMD extension aliasing the x87 register file.

entities.name: 3DNow!
entities.description: AMD packed single-precision floating-point extension; historical and now obsolete.

entities.name: SSE
entities.description: 128-bit XMM SIMD extension initially focused on single-precision floating point.

entities.name: SSE2
entities.description: Extends SSE with double-precision floating point and packed integer operations.

entities.name: SSE3
entities.description: Additional SIMD, memory, and thread-related instructions introduced in later Pentium 4-era processors.

entities.name: SSSE3
entities.description: Supplemental packed integer and byte-shuffle operations.

entities.name: SSE4.1
entities.description: Additional packed integer, blend, dot-product and conversion operations.

entities.name: SSE4.2
entities.description: Additional string comparison and CRC32 instructions.

entities.name: AES-NI
entities.description: Instructions accelerating AES encryption/decryption transformations.

entities.name: PCLMULQDQ / CLMUL
entities.description: Carry-less multiplication useful for polynomial arithmetic and cryptographic algorithms.

entities.name: AVX
entities.description: 256-bit vector extension using VEX encoding and YMM register views.

entities.name: AVX2
entities.description: Expands AVX to more packed-integer operations and gather/shuffle capabilities.

entities.name: FMA3/FMA
entities.description: Fused multiply-add operations combining multiplication and addition with a single rounding step.

entities.name: F16C
entities.description: Half-precision floating-point conversion instructions.

entities.name: BMI1
entities.description: Bit manipulation instructions such as ANDN, BEXTR, BLSI/BLSMSK/BLSR.

entities.name: BMI2
entities.description: Bit manipulation instructions including MULX, PDEP, PEXT, and variable bit shifts.

entities.name: ADX
entities.description: Extended-precision addition instructions ADCX and ADOX with separate carry chains.

entities.name: AVX-512
entities.description: Family of 512-bit vector extensions with EVEX encoding, opmask registers, and feature subsets.

entities.name: AVX-VNNI
entities.description: Vector neural-network instructions for dot-product style integer operations.

entities.name: AVX-IFMA
entities.description: AVX vector integer fused multiply-add instructions for selected integer widths.

entities.name: AVX10
entities.description: Vector ISA initiative intended to provide a more consistent scalable vector feature model across supported processors.

entities.name: Intel AMX
entities.description: Tile/matrix acceleration instructions requiring supporting architectural state and OS enablement.

entities.name: Intel APX
entities.description: Advanced Performance Extensions proposal/feature family including additional GPRs, new encodings and instruction forms; exact availability is processor-specific.

entities.name: Intel VT-x / VMX
entities.description: Intel hardware virtualization facilities including VM entry/exit and VMCS-managed guest state.

entities.name: Intel VT-d
entities.description: I/O virtualization and DMA remapping platform technology, distinct from the CPU instruction ISA itself.

entities.name: AMD-V / SVM
entities.description: AMD hardware virtualization facilities for guest execution and control.

entities.name: AMD-Vi / IOMMU
entities.description: I/O memory management and DMA remapping platform facilities.

entities.name: Intel SGX
entities.description: Enclave-based isolation feature supported only on selected processors/platforms.

entities.name: Intel TSX
entities.description: Transactional synchronization extensions on implementations where enabled and available.

entities.name: Control-flow Enforcement Technology
entities.description: Control-flow protection features including shadow stacks and indirect branch tracking on supported processors.

entities.name: RDRAND
entities.description: Instruction returning hardware-generated random data when supported and successful.

entities.name: RDSEED
entities.description: Instruction providing seed-quality random data where supported.

entities.name: SHA extensions
entities.description: Instructions accelerating selected SHA cryptographic computations.

entities.name: SM3/SM4 extensions
entities.description: Optional instruction support for SM3 and SM4 cryptographic algorithms on some processors.

entities.name: Intel MPX
entities.description: Historical bounds-checking extension; deprecated/removed in many environments.

entities.name: AMD XOP
entities.description: Historical AMD vector extension using XOP encoding; not widely supported across vendors.

entities.name: AVX-VNNI-INT8 and related variants
entities.description: Selected vector neural-network integer operation variants, availability dependent on CPU feature set.

entities.name: FRED
entities.description: Flexible Return and Event Delivery, a modernized event/interrupt delivery mechanism discussed in the ecosystem standardization context.

entities.name: ChkTag / memory tagging initiative
entities.description: Memory-tagging-related x86 ecosystem initiative; exact product availability and specification depend on implementation.

entities.name: ACE matrix initiative
entities.description: Ecosystem initiative concerning matrix-multiplication acceleration; distinguish proposals/standardization from universally available hardware.

entities.name: Global Descriptor Table (GDT)
entities.description: Table of segment and system descriptors used in protected-mode execution.

entities.name: Local Descriptor Table (LDT)
entities.description: Optional local descriptor table selected through LDTR.

entities.name: Interrupt Descriptor Table (IDT)
entities.description: Table of interrupt/trap gates and exception handlers.

entities.name: Page tables
entities.description: Hierarchical structures mapping linear addresses to physical frames and applying permissions.

entities.name: Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB)
entities.description: Caches address-translation results to reduce page-table-walk cost.

entities.name: Physical address
entities.description: Address presented to physical memory/platform after translation.

entities.name: Linear address
entities.description: Address produced by segmentation; paging may translate it to a physical address.

entities.name: Virtual address
entities.description: Process-visible address space abstraction, commonly mapped by OS paging.

entities.name: Physical memory / RAM
entities.description: Memory addressed by the platform's physical address space.

entities.name: Virtual memory
entities.description: Per-process or system address-space abstraction backed by page tables and OS policy.

entities.name: Page fault (#PF)
entities.description: Exception raised when a memory access violates translation or permission rules or requires OS handling.

entities.name: General protection fault (#GP)
entities.description: Protection-related exception raised for various invalid or disallowed operations.

entities.name: Invalid opcode (#UD)
entities.description: Exception raised when an instruction encoding or feature use is invalid/unavailable in the current context.

entities.name: Divide error (#DE)
entities.description: Exception from integer division error conditions.

entities.name: System call
entities.description: Controlled transition from user application to OS kernel service.

entities.name: Interrupt/exception handler
entities.description: Kernel or firmware routine dispatched for a supported interrupt or exception.

entities.name: Hypervisor
entities.description: Software controlling guest virtual machines using virtualization extensions or software techniques.

entities.name: Guest virtual machine
entities.description: Virtualized operating-system instance whose execution state is controlled by a hypervisor.

entities.name: VMCS / virtual-machine control structure
entities.description: Intel VMX structure controlling guest/host state and VM-exit behavior.

entities.name: VMCB / virtual-machine control block
entities.description: AMD SVM control structure for guest state and intercepts.

entities.name: ELF object/executable format
entities.description: Object and executable format commonly used on Linux and many Unix-like systems.

entities.name: PE/COFF format
entities.description: Windows executable and object-file format family.

entities.name: Mach-O format
entities.description: Executable/object format used by Apple operating systems.

entities.name: COFF object format
entities.description: Common Object File Format family used in various toolchains and platforms.

entities.name: Relocation
entities.description: Linker/loader fixup describing how an address-dependent field is adjusted.

entities.name: Symbol table entry
entities.description: Named function/object or other symbol referenced and resolved during assembly/linking.

entities.name: Object file
entities.description: Assembler/compiler output containing code/data sections, symbols, and relocations.

entities.name: Executable image
entities.description: Linked program image prepared for loading and execution.

entities.name: Shared library
entities.description: Dynamically loaded code/data object, often using position-independent code.

entities.name: Position-independent code (PIC)
entities.description: Code designed to execute correctly when loaded at different virtual addresses; RIP-relative addressing helps on x86-64.

entities.name: Calling convention
entities.description: Rules assigning arguments/returns to registers or stack and defining caller/callee-saved state.

entities.name: System V AMD64 ABI
entities.description: Common x86-64 ABI used on many Unix-like systems; exact details are platform ABI specification.

entities.name: Microsoft x64 calling convention
entities.description: Windows x64 calling convention with its own argument registers, shadow space, and preservation rules.

UMIP restricts selected system-information instructions in user mode.
Effective protection requires OS configuration and correct privilege/state management.
Some security properties and vulnerabilities depend on implementation details.

Atom is an Intel processor family.
Zhaoxin products implement x86-compatible processors.
Linux supports x86 and x86-64 platforms.

Intel manuals document instruction/system architecture.
AMD manuals document AMD64 architecture.
CPUID and related mechanisms expose feature information.
Runtime dispatch can choose an appropriate compiler-generated code path.
Compilers may emit vector instructions when target features and optimization allow.
Compilers may emit cryptographic instructions under target-feature controls.
Compilers lower atomic operations into architecture-specific instructions/sequences.
Legacy port I/O exists in applicable modes, subject to privilege/platform constraints.
Architectural interrupts and exceptions transfer control through mode-specific mechanisms.
x86 multi-byte scalar values use little-endian byte order.
The architecture uses little-endian byte order for scalar memory representations.
Most ordinary x86 memory instructions permit unaligned addresses, though performance and atomicity constraints vary.
Unaligned access can incur penalties or cross-boundary effects depending on instruction and microarchitecture.
Instruction encodings vary in length from 1 to 15 bytes.
Many instructions allow one explicit memory operand alongside a register or immediate operand.
x86 retains register-memory instruction forms despite modern internal execution techniques.
PAE changes paging structures, not the width of the virtual/linear address.
NX/XD is a page permission bit used by operating systems for execute prevention.
MMX added packed integer SIMD to selected Pentium-generation processors.
SSE was introduced in 1999-era processors.
SSE2 became a baseline feature for x86-64 architectural environments.
AVX introduced YMM-width vector views and VEX encoding.
AVX2 expanded integer SIMD operations.
AVX-512 is a family of subsets, not a universal feature of every x86 CPU.
AMX requires processor support and operating-system management of tile state.
APX availability must be verified per processor and toolchain; not universal across x86.
VMX requires privileged setup and hypervisor handling.
SVM requires privileged setup and hypervisor handling.
CET availability and enforcement depend on processor, OS, and process policy.

AMD introduced 3DNow! in 1997.

AMD-V/SVM arrived in the 2005-era processor generation.
